chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Ja‘far al-Bāqir عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who witnesses the accounting between two men, then is called to testify, he عليه السلام said: “If he wishes, he may testify, and if he wishes, he may refrain from testifying.”

key_terms.حِسَابَ: the reckoning or accounting of a matter, especially financial dealings
key_terms.لَمْ يَشْهَدْ: he did not testify or refrained from testifying

ai.seo_question: Is a person who knows of a transaction between two people required to testify when called?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about someone who has direct knowledge of a financial reckoning between two people and is later asked to give testimony. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام states that in this case, giving testimony is left to his choice, indicating permissibility rather than obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3322 - Al-Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), regarding a man who observes the accounting between two men and is then called to testify.
Imam (as) said: "If he wishes, he may testify, and if he wishes, he may abstain from testifying."
